label: candidate_against_proposed
description: Status observation and coverage at one authorization boundary. Two status sources a verifier trusts disagree about the same delegation, a source answers past its declared freshness bound, and a verifier that declared itself offline admits on a snapshot inside a bound it declared in advance. Every case is a candidate against proposed text. Nothing here is a conformance claim about APS or any published specification.

proposed_text.note: The text under test, not an external source for any claim. Cited by section name and commit so a reader can pin what this fixture was written against.

determinism.digest: SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 canonical bytes of the status-observation record
determinism.clock: every instant is a constant in generate.ts; no wall-clock read anywhere
determinism.chain: chain.json, minted by mint.py from the same seed_input

reasons.status_active_all_sources_agree: admit; every required source answered inside its freshness bound and every answer was active
reasons.status_revoked: deny; a source the verifier trusts answered revoked and no usable answer disagreed
reasons.status_sources_conflict: deny; two sources the verifier trusts gave different determinate answers about the same delegation
reasons.status_stale_beyond_bound: not_established; an answer the verdict needed was older than the bound declared for its source
reasons.status_coverage_incomplete: not_established; a source the trust policy requires produced no answer at all
reasons.status_no_usable_observation: not_established; no source produced a usable determinate answer
reasons.admitted_on_snapshot_within_declared_bou: admit; an offline verifier used a snapshot inside the bound it declared, and recorded which snapshot and what age

controls.name: drop-stale-then-decide
controls.axis: what survives the freshness bound, and what coverage is measured over

controls.name: offline-admit-without-recording
controls.axis: whether an offline admission records the snapshot and age it used

cases.label: candidate_against_proposed
cases.description: The negative control a naive implementation passes wrongly. The revoked answer is past its source freshness bound and the active answer is inside its own, so an implementation that discards stale answers before deciding sees one fresh active answer and admits. A revocation that was observed does not become unobserved with age, so the reference verifier still counts it and the states still conflict.

draft_03.note: draft-03 Section 3.3 states that an unavailable or stale revocation result is indeterminate, and that a caller must not collapse indeterminate into valid. It does not define a per-source freshness bound, and it does not state what the result is when one source is stale and another is fresh, so the boundary verdict this case checks is not a draft-03 conformance case. draft-03 Section 3.5 does state that revocation is irreversible, which is why an observed revocation is still counted here, but it states nothing about weighing it against a fresher answer from a second source.
